To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Eysencks Personality Questionnaire is an effective measure of the three dimensions of personality that Eysenck postulated, that it is possible to identify the items of the Eysensck questionnaire which are most effective in measuring each dimension, and that the most accurate measurement of each dimension is obtained from the best possible short form of the questionnaire, of length 10 items.
the Eysencks' personality questionnaire is best described as a 4-factor model, with the factors being Neuroticism, Extraversion, Psychoticism, and Social Desirability.
(a) the Eysencks' model of personality is not supported by the present data, and (b) the best possible short forms of the EPQ consist of 10 items each.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of questionnaires with binary items, and the development of short forms of such instruments.
the analysis of the EPPQ, and the development of a short form of it which provides accurate measurement of the underlying latent traits of extraversion, neuroticism and psychoticism.
the development of a psychometric model that is capable of handling dichotomous responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EPQ has been shown to measure three latent traits, Extraversion, Neuroticism and Psychoticism, with a reasonable level of precision, and with a good deal of consistency across the three forms of the questionnaire, the EPQ-R, the EPQ-E, and the EPQ-P.
the EPQ is a well constructed instrument, with high reliability, good construct validity and high internal consistency.
the Eysencks have produced a questionnaire which, in the hands of the skilled user, is a powerful tool for the assessment of individual personality traits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EPQ has a good deal to recommend it.
the Latent Trait Model provides an extremely useful and flexible framework for analysing the psychometric properties of dichotomous questionnaires.
, with the exception of the Lie scale, the Eysencks' questionnaire is a very good instrument for measurement of the three personality traits that it purports to measure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Eysencks EPQ is a good instrument for measuring the traits of Neuroticism, Extraversion, Psychoticism, and Lie.

the Eysencks' personality inventory, which was designed to measure the three dimensions of extraversion, neuroticism, and psychoticism, is actually measuring a single dimension, with the psychoticism scale being a misfit to the data.

it is possible to obtain accurate estimates of the precision of individual items, in a questionnaire with dichotomously-scored items, and that the resulting information is useful in the construction of short forms.
